definition: A large family of related languages spoken across much of sub-Saharan Africa, including Kongo, Zulu, Luba and Ganda. It is a linguistic category, not a religion or a single culture, so 'Bantu mythology' is a misleading phrase.

A people of the lower Congo River region, in what is now the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Republic of the Congo and Angola. Their traditions include the creator Nzambi Mpungu and the Kingdom of Kongo, which adopted Christianity in the late fifteenth century.
A people of the Ituri rainforest in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Their heroic epic of Mwindo was recorded by Daniel Biebuyck from the bard Candi Rureke and published in 1969.

A cluster of peoples in the Katanga region of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, known for the Luba kingdom and its sacred kingship. Their foundation narratives centre on Mbidi Kiluwe and his son Kalala Ilunga.
The people of Buganda, in what is now Uganda, on the northern shore of Lake Victoria. Ganda tradition preserves the story of Kintu and Nambi, recorded in detail by the missionary John Roscoe in 1911.

A people of what is now KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa, speakers of isiZulu. Zulu tradition includes Unkulunkulu and the chameleon's message, collected by nineteenth-century writers such as Henry Callaway.

The Kongo creator, often called Nzambi Mpungu. The name is used for God in modern Kikongo, a usage shaped by Christian translation, and the creator is usually understood as distant from everyday affairs.
The Zulu creator and first ancestor, whose name means 'the very great old one'. He is said to have come from a reed and to have made the first people, and the name later became the Zulu word for God.

The hero of a Nyanga epic. Born walking and talking, he quarrels with his father, descends to the underworld, returns, and becomes chief; the epic is performed by bards and was recorded by Daniel Biebuyck.
The title of the female ruler of the Balobedu in Limpopo province, South Africa. The queen's authority is both political and ritual, and her rain-making is a living tradition rather than a lost myth.
